deck.title: ElastiCache
deck.analogy: A cache is a sticky note on the librarian's front desk: answer repeated questions instantly instead of consulting the binder (database) every time.

subtopics.title: Redis vs Memcached — the only table you need

cards.front: What is an ElastiCache cache and why is it faster than the database?

back.answer: It keeps answers to repeated queries in RAM, roughly 1000x faster than disk-based database queries.
back.explanation: Response times drop from milliseconds to microseconds and the database does less work.
back.mnemonic: A sticky note on the front desk instead of walking to the binder.

cards.front: Which two engines does ElastiCache run?

back.answer: Redis or Memcached, managed with patching, monitoring and failover handled for you.

cards.front: ElastiCache vs DAX: which requires application code changes?

back.answer: ElastiCache requires code changes (app must check cache first); DAX is DynamoDB API-compatible and needs none.
back.explanation: The exam loves this distinction.

cards.front: What is the ElastiCache request flow on a hit vs a miss?

back.answer: Hit: return from cache in microseconds. Miss: query database, write result into cache, return.
back.explanation: The next asker then gets the cached answer.
back.code:
App → check cache → hit: return
                  → miss: query DB → write to cache → return

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: persistence?

back.answer: Redis persists data across restarts; Memcached does not.

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: replication and Multi-AZ automatic failover?

back.answer: Redis supports replication and Multi-AZ automatic failover; Memcached does not.

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: backup and restore?

back.answer: Redis supports backup and restore; Memcached does not.

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: sorted sets?

back.answer: Redis supports sorted sets (leaderboards); Memcached does not.

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: pub/sub messaging?

back.answer: Redis supports pub/sub; Memcached does not.

cards.front: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached: which is multi-threaded and dead-simple?

back.answer: Memcached is multi-threaded and simple; Redis is not.
back.explanation: Memcached wins only when the cache is simplest, loss is acceptable and multithreading is wanted.

cards.sourceHeading: Redis vs Memcached — the only table you need

cards.front: Rule of thumb for choosing between ElastiCache Redis and Memcached?

back.answer: Any grown-up feature (durability, failover, backup, leaderboard, pub/sub) → Redis; simplest, loss OK, multithreaded → Memcached.
back.explanation: Redis wins about 90% of exam appearances.

cards.front: Why does ElastiCache Redis suit a real-time gaming leaderboard?

back.answer: Sorted sets keep members ordered by score automatically, so top-10 lookups are instant.

cards.front: What is the exam giveaway phrase for the ElastiCache session store pattern?

back.answer: "Users are logged out when instances are terminated/scaled in."
back.explanation: Sessions stored in an instance's own memory vanish when the ASG terminates it.

cards.front: How do you fix users being logged out when an ASG scales in, using ElastiCache?

back.answer: Make the web tier stateless by storing sessions in ElastiCache for Redis (or DynamoDB).
back.explanation: Any server can then handle any request.

cards.front: What is lazy loading (cache-aside) in ElastiCache?

back.answer: Populate the cache on a read miss; only data actually requested is cached.
back.explanation: Efficient for hot data, but can serve stale data and every miss pays a penalty.
back.mnemonic: Writing a cheat sheet during the exam.

cards.front: What is write-through caching with ElastiCache and its trade-off?

back.answer: Update the cache on every database write: never stale, reads always hit, but double writes and unread data cached.

cards.front: What does a TTL do on ElastiCache cached entries?

back.answer: Stale data expires automatically after N seconds — a middle ground between strategies.

cards.front: Trap: ElastiCache and "stale data is unacceptable" (prices, inventory)?

back.explanation: Lazy loading can serve stale data when the database changes underneath.

cards.front: Repeated, identical reads hammering the database: which service?

back.explanation: The same product page read 10,000x belongs in memory.

cards.front: Diverse, complex or analytical read queries: ElastiCache or Read Replica?

back.explanation: Each query differs, so a cache would never hit.

cards.front: DynamoDB reads plus "no code changes": which service?
Trap: "month-end reporting queries slow down the app" — use ElastiCache?

back.explanation: Reporting queries are all different, so a cache never hits.

cards.front: Popular product pages generate thousands of identical reads that overload RDS. Best fix?

back.explanation: Repeated reads belong in memory.

choices.why: Better for diverse queries, not identical repeats.
Repeated identical reads are served from memory.
Does not address repeated read load.

cards.front: Real-time gaming leaderboard with player rankings. Which ElastiCache feature?

back.explanation: Ranking is built in.

choices.why: A strategy, not a ranking feature.

cards.front: Users get logged out when the Auto Scaling Group terminates instances. Fix?

back.answer: Store sessions in ElastiCache for Redis.
back.explanation: Makes the web tier stateless.

choices.text: Store sessions in ElastiCache for Redis

choices.why: Local cache is lost with the instance.

cards.front: Cache must survive a node failure without data loss. Which engine?

back.explanation: Replication + Multi-AZ failover; Memcached has neither.

cards.front: Simplest cache, multithreaded, losing cached data is fine. Which engine?

back.explanation: The only time it wins.

cards.front: Cached prices must never be out of date. Which caching strategy?

back.explanation: Cache updated on every write; lazy loading can serve stale.

choices.why: Cache updated on every database write.

cards.front: Long analytical/reporting queries slow the production database. Best option?

back.explanation: Diverse queries never hit cache.

choices.why: Diverse queries never hit the cache.

cards.front: Speed up DynamoDB reads without modifying the application. Which service?

back.explanation: ElastiCache would require code changes.

cards.front: Publish/subscribe messaging between app components using the cache layer. Which engine?

back.explanation: Pub/sub is Redis-only.

choices.why: Pub/sub is supported only in Redis.
